title: The Autonomous Enterprise, Unfiltered: Lessons From 16 Executive Conversations
summary: From SAP, the Autonomous Enterprise Podcast delivers candid conversations on AI adoption: 16 episodes of real customers, actionable insights.
body_markdown:
Since[SAP Sapphire in May](https://news.sap.com/2026/05/sap-sapphire-sap-unveils-autonomous-enterprise/) , SAP CEO Christian Klein has positioned the Autonomous Enterprise as the operating model for organizations that will lead the decade ahead, a model in which AI agents reason, decide, and execute inside the workflows that run the business.


For many enterprise leaders, however, the gap between strategic ambition and operational reality has remained frustratingly wide. That gap is exactly what the Autonomous Enterprise podcast set out to close.

Launched on June 1, 2026, the weekly series has now published 16 episodes spanning three format categories: SAP Deep Dives, with executive leaders on strategy and product; Customer Deep Dives, with companies narrating their own transformation journeys; and Industry Deep Dives, with selected external voices shaping entire industries.


Available on Spotify, Apple Music, and all major podcast platforms, as well as on SAP channels and LinkedIn, the show has rapidly established itself as a direct and candid voice on enterprise AI adoption.


## **What the first 16 episodes reveal**


Across more than a dozen conversations—with guests that include SAP executives, global customers, and external thought leaders—four themes emerge with striking consistency.


### **Autonomous enterprise is available today, not tomorrow**


In episode 13, Uma Rani, president and chief product officer for SAP Cloud ERP Private, plainly stated that the Autonomous Enterprise is not a future road map item; it is available now for customers on the 2025 and 2023 releases. The show’s earliest episodes reinforced this framing: Peter Maier, leading Strategic Customer Engagements in the Office of the CEO, opened episode one by grounding the SAP Sapphire vision in practical execution, while Manoj Swaminathan used episode three to unpack the architecture of SAP Autonomous Suite, the layer where AI assistants and agents begin to execute end-to-end processes.


### **The decisive advantage is business context, not model capability**


Michael Ameling, formerly president of the SAP Business AI Platform at SAP, explained in episode four how SAP Knowledge Graph and domain models, combined with frontier models including Anthropic’s Claude, give enterprise AI the semantic grounding that generic LLMs lack. The platform brings together 50 years of SAP process knowledge to enable agents that act relevantly, reliably, and responsibly—three conditions every guest returned to when discussing trustworthy AI at scale.


### **Transformation is a people and change management challenge as much as a technology one**


In episode two, Ferose V R articulated a shift from humans adapting to systems toward systems adapting to humans, through agents that understand context and intent. Sanjay Kulkarni, senior vice president and global head of Global Delivery Hub at SAP, brought a practitioner’s precision to episode 12: his 12,500-strong services organization measures AI value not by deployment volume, but by measurable business outcomes and the readiness of the people responsible for them. The same message came from Geoff Scott, CEO and chief community champion of Americas’ SAP Users’ Group (ASUG), in episode eight: trust, skill development, and genuine human-AI collaboration are the variables that separate transformations that scale from those that stall.


### **Geographic diversity shapes adoption, but the direction is universal**


In episode nine, SAP Labs India Managing Director Sindhu Gangadharan mapped how Indian enterprises are approaching autonomous capabilities: fast adoption, high ambition, and a particular emphasis on workforce readiness. Manos Raptopoulos, global president of Customer Success, Europe, APAC, Middle East, and Africa, covered in episode 11 what AI ambition looks like from Frankfurt to Fukuoka, illustrating how regional context varies while the structural imperatives remain the same. And SAP EMEA President Augusta Spinelli used episode five to define the two concrete paths to the Autonomous Enterprise—RISE with SAP and SAP GROW—as well as what agent-led transformation looks like from an execution standpoint.


In addition, customer episodes add the texture that strategy alone cannot provide. Achim Loebke from Uniper and Daniele Tedesco from Essity both shared in-depth, unfiltered accounts of what AI transformation looks like from the inside, including the organizational friction, the decisions that require human judgment, and the early indicators of measurable impact. These conversations, deliberately not positioned as product showcases, have consistently drawn the highest listener engagement.


## **Why this series matters for the SAP ecosystem**


The Autonomous Enterprise podcast fills a gap by offering candid, executive-level conversations where the honest complexity of AI adoption is treated as the point, not a problem to be managed. Its target audience—CIOs, CDOs, COOs, CFOs, and senior transformation leads—are precisely the people making the investment and governance decisions that will determine how quickly SAP customers move from AI ambition to AI execution.


With more than 40 episodes planned for its first year, the series is building a cumulative body of insight that serves both as a reference for practitioners navigating their own transformation journeys and as evidence of the breadth and depth of SAP’s engagement with its customer community.


New episodes drop weekly; listen on Spotify, Apple Music, and all major podcast platforms.


---


Benedikt Gieger is Product Strategy and AI lead in Digital Manufacturing at SAP SE.
Julia Kloppenburg is a technology consultant in Customer Engagement & Adoption at SAP SE.
